articles.content: In an outcome seen as a backlash to President Donald Trump, Democrats decisively won control of the U.S. Senate and the House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections . The Dems’ win of the House was called by MS NOW just before 10 p.m. ET followed by CNN several minutes later, then NBC News and CBS News. articles.title: The Mad (Color) Science Behind Rian Johnson’s New Camera App
articles.summary: Steve Yedlin talks to IndieWire about designing the Chromagraph app and bullying the iPhone camera to behave more cinematically — with math!
articles.content: You shouldn’t ever take a photo of your midterm election ballot — it’s illegal in some states — but, thanks to Rian Johnson and his longtime DP Steve Yedlin , there is now a very cinematic way to take iPhone photos of everything else. Yedlin has spent more than 20 years as a cinematographer, collaborating closely with Johnson on everything from “Brick” and “The Brothers Bloom” to “ The Last Jedi ” and the “ Knives Out ” films. But Yedlin has also spent 20 years delving into the science of color and how filmmakers can better craft imagery through the technical tools available. And now he and his friends are in the business of making new ones. Related Stories 5 Big Challenges in Creating Criterion’s ‘The Complete Kubrick’: From Navigating HDR/4K to Preserving Stanley Kubrick’s Love of Mono Sound Ebenezer’s Venmo and ‘How to Rob a Bank’ ATMs: Studios Are Now Promoting Movies by Just Giving Away Money Yedlin, Johnson, and color science coder Eric Cameron have been in the process of creating new software for light controls to replace traditional dimmer boards, pixel mapping, and on-screen playback (ie., when actors are looking at phone or computer screens on camera) with something that embraces the world of color-tunable lights and LEDs. But as a side project, they’ve also just launched Chromagraph, an iPhone app that uses Yedlin’s deep, mathematical understanding of color to bypass the iPhone’s default photo processing settings for a more filmic look. The app project started because Johnson wanted something on his phone that could capture photos the way that Yedlin captures film — using RAW images (ie., everything the sensor captures, not just what’s rendered on a screen) and bypassing the standard iPhone image processing protocols. articles.title: Ebenezer’s Venmo and ‘How to Rob a Bank’ ATMs: Studios Are Now Promoting Movies by Just Giving Away Money
articles.summary: Film marketing teams are creating stunts around cold, hard cash — a bid at virality built for the internet's bleak age of endless transactions.
articles.content: Clipfarming, influencer screenings, and meme-bait popcorn buckets: promoting a movie in the internet age is often a full-court offensive to get noticed. In that spirit, why not just get down to business and resort to modern civilization’s oldest method for seeking attention: dangling some money in people’s faces? That’s what the marketing teams behind “ How to Rob a Bank ,” from Amazon MGM Studios , and “ Ebenezer ,” from Skydance’s Paramount Pictures , have tried in the weeks leading up to their shared November 13 release to North American theaters. For the former ensemble heist thriller, a branded ATM was moved between multiplexes throughout the Los Angeles area over the course of four days. Those who learned of the campaign on the film ‘s social media channels could gain clues about the machine’s location and a specified PIN number, which would spark payouts of a single one-hundred-dollar bill to those who bothered to seek out (or stumble upon) it. articles.title: Netflix Launches First AI-Branded Content Recommendations Feature on TVs
articles.content: Initial test of feature will be available on select smart televisions in the U.S. Netflix , which has seen viewer engagement slide in recent quarters, is turning to AI for a new feature aimed at spurring users to find something new to watch. The company on Tuesday (Nov. 3) is debuting AI Discover, a new feature on the Netflix TV app, initially to a limited number of subscribers in the U.S. In the first iteration of the new AI-based tool, you are prompted to explore content based on preset themes (such as “Something Light,” “Scare Me,” “Workplace Comedy Favorites,” “Family Movie Night,” “Quick Watches,” “Family Scandal Sagas” or “Royal Court Intrigue”). The recommended titles are produced in real time, according to Netflix, based on a user’s viewing history and preferences as well as what’s trending on the platform. Related Stories Did Karen Bass Expand Film Incentives? Nithya Raman Campaign Flags 'Whopper' Claim California Tried to Jumpstart the Film Economy. Production Keeps Falling. The streamer will begin rolling out AI Discover in the U.S. to customers who use Netflix in English on supported smart TVs. If you have access to it, you will see a “Discover” tab with a red gem-shaped icon and a “New” label in the top navigation bar on your TV. The company plans to expand the feature to more regions and customers in the coming weeks. Netflix has long used machine-learning and AI technologies to personalize content recommendations, but AI Discover is the first user-facing application that the company is branding as powered by artificial intelligence. The hope is that the AI-recommended titles will be another tool to drive up Netflix’s total watch time among viewers, especially in the U.S. Amid a recent drop-off in per-subscriber viewing, Netflix overhauled its content leadership team, which included replacing content chief Bela Bajaria with industry veteran Peter Rice in a bid to produce more hits. articles.content: An anonymous U.K. celebrity has lost his injunction bid to prevent two news organizations from publishing sexual misconduct allegations against him and therefore revealing his identity. Earlier this month, it was reported that an anonymous celebrity had applied for a permanent injunction at London’s High Court to try to stop ITN and The Guardian from publishing a story containing allegations that he abused his power to engage in “inappropriate sexual activities with a large number of girls and young women,” according to BBC News. The celebrity denies the allegations. Judge Mr. Justice Nicklin rejected the injunction request on Tuesday, as reported by BBC News , but the celebrity will remain anonymous for the time being to allow him a chance to appeal the judgement. “The claimant’s claim for an injunction was dismissed,” Nicklin said in his ruling. However, he added: “The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make.” The lawyer for the celebrity told the court earlier that should he lose the injunction and the stories publish, it was “highly likely” he would attempt to commit suicide. According to his lawyer, he has already attempted to do so twice before. ITN and The Guardian’s lawyer, on the other hand, argued that publishing the allegations and the man’s identity is in the public’s best interest. He said that the news organizations had spoken to over 100 people in their investigation and that many of the women “have been traumatized by the claimant’s alleged conduct and have suffered mental health crises and mental illness as a result,” according to BBC News. Jason Statham and Guy Ritchie Reunite — Again — for Netflix Revenge Action Movie 'Dogfight'

Jason Statham and Guy Ritchie Reunite — Again — for Netflix Revenge Action Movie 'Dogfight'
articles.content: The Jason Statham – Guy Ritchie partnership is set to extend into a seventh film. “Dogfight” — announced by Netflix — is described as a “stylish revenge actioner” set in the London criminal underworld. No other plot details have been revealed, but it’s safe to presume there’ll be guns, blood and — probably — some mean-looking faces. Production is due to commence n early 2027, with filming taking place in the U.K. Like almost all of their previous collaborations, Ritchie will write, direct and produce, while Statham will star. Production companies on “Dogfight” are Black Bear Pictures, behind most of Ritchie’s recent titles (including his latest releases “In the Grey” and “Wife & Dog”) plus Ritchie’s own Toff Guy Films and Statham’s Punch Palace Productions. Producers include Ritchie, Statham, Ritchie’s Toff Guy partner Ivan Atkinson and John Friedberg from Black Bear. “Dogfight” lengthens a long-running and hugely successful relationship between the director and his action star, which began when Ritchie gave Statham his first film role in his 1998 directorial debut “Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels.” This partnership would continue with “Snatch,” “Revolver,” “Wrath of Man” and “Operation Fortune: Rose de Guerre.” The pair’s latest feature together, announced last year by Variety , is the action-thriller “Viva La Madness,” based on J.J. Connolly’s novel and the author’s sequel to “Layer Cake,” which was adapted into the 2004 film by Matthew Vaughn. However, while plot details have been kept under wraps, “Viva La Madness” has been described as a standalone film and not a continuation of previous work. Principal photography on the film wrapped earlier this year, with Black Bear distributing in North America and Amazon MGM Studios holding rights to most international territories.

articles.content: Two years after merging, Jason Blum ‘s Blumhouse and James Wan ‘s Atomic Monster will now call their combined entity Blumhouse Atomic . articles.content: Jason Statham will star in Dogfight , a new Netflix feature written, directed, and produced by Guy Ritchie . The streamer has said production is slated to begin in early 2027, with filming taking place in the UK. The production companies are Black Bear, Toff Guy Films, and Punch Palace. Producing alongside Ritchie are Statham, Ivan Atkinson, and John Friedberg. The film is described as a “stylish revenge actioner set in the London criminal underworld.” Dogfight will be the seventh film collaboration between Ritchie and Statham. Their film credits include Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels , Snatch, and the upcoming film Viva La Madness. Viva La Madness is based on the novel of the same name by J.J. Connolly, who co-wrote the screenplay for the film adaptation with Ritchie. Watch on Deadline Connolly’s debut novel, Layer Cake , was previously adapted for the screen by Matthew Vaughn. Viva La Madness was developed by Statham for Punch Palace Productions and Thomas Benski for Lumina Studios, who are producing alongside Ritchie and Ivan Atkinson for Toff Guy Films and John Friedberg for Black Bear. Black Bear will distribute the film domestically, while Amazon MGM Studios will distribute it in the majority of international territories. articles.title: Doc Talk Podcast: Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival’s Ken Jacobson On State Of Nonfiction Filmmaking, Competitive Oscar Race And More
articles.content: Hot Springs, Arkansas is known for many things – as the childhood home of Bill Clinton, as the former site of Major League Baseball’s spring training (in the era of Babe Ruth), for its beautiful national park, and for its mineral springs and the splendid early 20th century bathhouses built to accommodate legions of spa-goers. It’s also known as the home of the Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival , the longest-running nonfiction cinematic event in North America. HSDFF celebrated its 35th edition last month, hosting a selection of world premieres and leading contenders in the Oscar race including Once Upon a Time in Harlem , 14th , NAZA , American Doctor , Closure , To Hold a Mountain , Jane Elliott Against the World and more. On the latest edition of Deadline’s Doc Talk podcast, we’re joined by the man in charge of the festival, Hot Springs Documentary Film Institute executive director Ken Jacobson . He tells us how the festival originally began in collaboration with the Motion Picture Academy as a way to showcase Oscar-nominated and Oscar-winning films. This year, HSDFF returned to those roots in a sense by partnering with Deadline for its first ever Documentary Roundtable of distinguished filmmakers in the awards race, a panel that included directors Biljana Tutorov, Poh Si Teng and Michał Marczak, and producer Liani Greaves. Watch on Deadline Hot Springs once again presented its Forum, but with a twist this year: it took place without the usual support of the Corporation for Public Broadcasting, because that important entity was defunded under pressure from the Trump administration. Jacobson, who has long experience in documentary festival programming, tells us about the biggest challenge he faces putting on a nine-day event and how he makes sure the festival attracts filmmakers from around the world while simultaneously showcasing work from the South and mid-South. He also shares insights on how the Academy Awards competition is shaping up as we near next month

articles.title: ‘Magic Atlas’ Review: Surreal, Shapeshifting Animation Is a Sometimes Mystifying Technical Marvel
articles.content: Sun Xun's decade-long project spans different illustration media, different materials, even different dimensions, but it's hard to find a real emotional foothold in the artist's heady and fragmented picture. There’s an increasingly undeniable hunger for the hand-crafted. As discourse around animation becomes more and more absorbed by anaesthetizing questions about AI, it becomes clearer that people who care about the medium are pushing for tactility and foregrounding real texture, materials imprinted with genuine human feeling. This feels especially true of Sun Xun ’s “ Magic Atlas ,” made over the course of a decade using a refreshingly unrestrained range of different materials and techniques: paint, pen and ink on paper, canvas and newspapers, woodcut, or indeed anything with which the director can bring this strange and dreamlike picture to life. articles.content: Former The Ellen DeGeneres Show executive producer Matthew Wright died Friday in what a GoFundMe campaign for his family calls an “unfathomable tragedy.” He was 52, according to reports. Wright died while working remotely in Los Angeles, according to the GoFundMe, while his family is in New York. Both Wright and his husband were “laid off this summer,” the GoFundMe states. “And the unexpected costs of getting Matt home, a funeral and a memorial are impossible for the family to bear,” the GoFundMe reads. “If Matt has ever made you laugh, said an encouraging word right when you needed it or ordered one too many appetizers for the enjoyment of the whole table, now is the time to repay the favor. Please donate what you can and share this with anyone who’s been in the orbit of Matt’s huge heart. And when you’re at dinner and see a sunset, know that Matt is looking down, loving you, but wildly disappointed in what you ordered.” Related Stories Music Marty Erlichman, Barbra Streisand's Longtime Manager, Dies at 97 TV Bobby Wright, 'McHale's Navy' Actor, Singer and Son of Kitty Wells, Dies at 84 DeGeneres posted a tearful video on Instagram Monday remembering Wright, who worked on her show from 2006 to its finale in 2022. “He was an amazing guy. He was funny. God, he made me laugh. He would surprise me with things that he did all the time. He was smart. He was kind. He was the part of our show that — I mean, everyone loved him. I loved him. And it’s just shocking — it’s shocking. We’re gonna miss him. He is and always will be the glue to our entire family at The Ellen Show .” DeGeneres also noted that Wright was close with former Ellen DJ Stephen “tWitch” Boss, who died in 2022 , saying she believes the two are now reunited in the afterlife, “dancing and laughing.” DeGeneres ended her tribute with a compilation of some of Wright’s funniest moments on her show, including a video of him jokingly admonishing restaurants for bringing too many appetizers to the table at once in

articles.title: Sharon Horgan Comedy ‘Youth’ Renewed for Second Season at HBO
articles.summary: The renewal comes on the heels of the show's first season finale.
articles.content: The renewal comes a day after the show’s season finale, which saw Horgan’s character, Alex, at a crossroads both personally and professionally. There’s no word yet on when a second season might arrive. “I’m so happy to get another opportunity to live out my emotional and biological crises on HBO,” Horgan said in a statement. “I can’t think of a better platform to air my UTI problems on. The response to Youth has been beyond what I could have hoped for. I’m so grateful for the response and the chance to work with this incredible cast and creative team once more.” Related Stories TV 'The Birds' Series With Sarah Snook in the Works at HBO TV Kordell Stewart Hopes His New HBO Documentary Lands Him in the NFL Hall of Fame Youth follows Horgan’s Alex, a 50-year-old divorcee, as she tries to get her love life back on track, deals with a teenage son (Aran Murphy) having trouble adjusting to young adulthood and attempts to keep her career moving forward. “In a way that only she can, Sharon has created a show that makes us howl with laughter and with tears — often in the same moment,” said Amy Gravitt, executive vp HBO Programming and head of comedy series for HBO and HBO Max. “Each performance in Youth is more delightful than the next. Along with our partners at Merman, we are so thrilled to have this brilliant ensemble back for another season.” The series also stars Rupert Friend, Sharlene Whyte and Robbie Gee. Horgan created Youth and writes and executive produces in addition to starring. Faye Dorn of Horgan’s Merman company, Jim Kleverweis, and Dawn Shadforth also exec produce. Shadforth directed four of the season’s eight episodes, while Jim O’Hanlon helmed the other four.

articles.title: Michael Wilbon Takes Leave From ESPN for Health Reasons
articles.summary: The 'Pardon the Interruption' host says he'll be off the air indefinitely.
articles.content: Long-time Pardon the Interruption host Michael Wilbon says he is taking a leave of absence from ESPN to deal with health issues. In a statement posted on X , Wilbon wrote he is taking “a trip to the injured list. Hopefully not an extended one. Struggles with multiple health issues in recent months lead me to take an indefinite leave of absence from my PTI and NBA duties at ESPN and ABC.” Wilbon has co-hosted Pardon the Interruption with Tony Kornheiser since the show’s inception in 2001, where the two former Washington Post sportswriters discuss and debate the day’s news. PTI celebrated its 25th anniversary in October. Related Stories Business Disney, WWE Ink Expanded Partnership TV 'Inside the NBA' Host Ernie Johnson Says This Is His Final Season Wilbon said on Kornheiser’s podcast Monday that he missed last week’s run of PTI due to feeling “exhausted — beyond exhuasted, lifeless” and that Kornheiser and others close to him had encouraged him to take some time away from the show and from ESPN’s NBA coverage, where he is a studio analyst. Wilbon noted that he is diabetic, saying that “The bill has come due from too many red eye flights and just the stuff that I had ignored. When you’re a diabetic person and you ignore some of these things, the bill comes due, and it’s a damn more expensive bill than it might be for other people.” ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro said in a statement that “Michael and his family have ESPN’s full support as he takes time away to focus on his health and well-being. He’s an important member of our ESPN team and widely respected by his peers, sports fans and so many others throughout our industry. We are here for Michael every step of the way and look forward to welcoming him back whenever he is ready.” Frequent PTI guest hosts Pablo Torre and Frank Isola will fill in for Wilbon this week, and the network’s roster of NBA analysts will cover his work on those shows.

articles.summary: Incumbent Mayor Karen Bass and Councilmember Nithya Raman polled neck and neck ahead of Election Night The post Where the Los Angeles Mayor’s Race Stands appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: Incumbent Mayor Karen Bass and Councilmember Nithya Raman polled neck and neck ahead of Election Night The Los Angeles mayoral race was too close to call after polling closed Tuesday night, with incumbent Mayor Karen Bass facing off with competitor Nithya Raman, the councilmember from Los Angeles City Council District 4. At the time of writing, with 50% of the votes counted, Bass held a narrow lead over Raman, securing 50.7% of the vote to Raman’s 49.3%. Bass fought to keep her spot as Los Angeles’s leader against Councilmember Raman in the general election on Tuesday, with the mayor hosting an election night party in Hollywood at the Loews Hotel and Raman hosting at the Greek Theater. The final poll from the UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies found the mayoral candidates neck and neck with 40% of likely L.A. voters said they supported Bass, while another 40% supported challenger Raman. The poll also found that about 20% of Angelenos were still undecided just a week before Election Day. For the incumbent, the poll comes as a sigh of relief after a September poll found Raman ahead with an 11-percentage-point lead. Bass had not led a poll since August. Polling closed in Los Angeles at 8 p.m., but the final results are unlikely to come in until later this week. During the pandemic, California began mailing every registered voter a ballot, giving every voter the option to mail-in their ballots. Those ballots require far more time to process than in-person ballots, often delaying the results. Bass gathered with supporters at the Loews Hotel in Hollywood at the L.A. County Democratic Party Election Night. articles.content: “MAGA extremists are on the run from sea to shining sea,” Rep. Hakeem Jeffries says With Democrats projected to win both the House and Senate after Tuesday’s midterms, many took to social media to celebrate the GOP’s loss as a “Republican Red Wedding.” The decisive wins across swing states including Texas and North Carolina delivered a major setback to President Donald Trump midway through his second term. The takeover will give Democrats the power to potentially block much of Trump’s legislative agenda, act as guard dogs for his administration and launch congressional investigations, ending two years of unified Republican control in Washington. Trump himself responded initially to the House flip shortly after it was reported by shuffling the blame away from himself. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump wrote on Truth Social . The president later congratulated Democrats in a statement to CBS News, saying that he’s looking forward to working with them. Democrats, meanwhile, celebrated nationwide and across social media. Political figures, media personalities and even popular influencers on platforms like X all celebrated and joked about what 2027 and beyond could look like with the Democrats overtaking Congress. “MAGA extremists are on the run from sea to shining sea,” House Minority Leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries wrote . “I’m not sure we’re mentally or emotionally ready for a lame duck Donald Trump,” “The View” co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin said . “Buckle up, folks.” Although it wasn’t just Democrats who marveled at the blue wave happening on election night. Meghan McCain kept it to just two words as she watched the night play out: “F–king bloodbath.” Here are more of the strongest and most noteworthy reactions from Democrats as the wins in the Senate and House continued rolling out. articles.content: The former California attorney general makes history as the first elected Latino governor of the Golden State, beating Republican Steve Hilton Xavier Becerra was named the winner of California’s gubernatorial race, making history as the first Latino elected governor of the state. “Ladies and gentlemen you have now entered the Becerra era,” the governor-elect said in his victory speech on Tuesday evening, adding: “Let me make something clear — I didn’t run to make history. I ran to make a difference.” AP News called the race in Becerra’s favor at exactly 8 p.m. PT Tuesday evening, writing, “The AP will only declare a winner at poll closing time in races not expected to be competitive when all available evidence points to an overwhelming victory. However, Becerra was already poised to beat his Republican competitor, according to polling from last week. In his victory speech, the politician emphasized, “Diversity is not our shortcoming, it’s our super power.” His victory was led by a crowd in Sacramento chanting, “Si se puede!,” which roughly translates to, “It is possible!” The poll from UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies and co-sponsored by the Los Angeles Times found the veteran Democratic politician would garner 61% of likely California voters, compared to 34% for the former Fox News commentator. Becerra has spent much of his career in public service. Most notably, the Democrat served as former President Joe Biden’s secretary of health and human services from 2021 to 2025. Before that, he served as California’s 33rd attorney general from 2017 to 2021 and as a U.S. representative from California from 1993 to 2017. Becerra was born and raised in California. articles.summary: The producer of Criterion's new Stanley Kubrick Box Set tells IndieWire about trying to get inside the mind of a director who was obsessed with his films' home video presentation.
articles.content: In 2024, archivist Michael Chaiken was approached by the Criterion Collection about what was being described as a “big Kubrick project.” It would start with remastering the director’s last film , “ Eyes Wide Shut, ” but for months the scope of the ambitious project remained an open question: Was a complete Stanley Kubrick box set even possible? Kubrick was a precise director, and his control over every aspect of his filmmaking process extended to its home video presentation. But home video technology has developed in ways (widescreen TVs, high dynamic range, 4K resolution, Dolby Atmos) that Kubrick could never have imagined before he died in 1999. Home video fanatics are often completists. articles.summary: From “The Devils” and David Lynch to a one-person erotic cinema and “Hardball,” here's how film programmers all across the U.S. are serving their communities on November 3.
articles.content: A provocation? A distraction? Something… else? Across our semi-united, Letterboxd-loving nation, new microcinemas are opening up , old movies are selling out, and local programmers are giving film fans tons of exciting reasons to hit the box office. This election cycle, the future of Hollywood remains an open question, as does the strength of our democracy. With control of Congress at stake, voters are debating what they want their country to become — and, in many cases, what they’re afraid it already is — to spectacular and exhausting effect. articles.summary: A Japanese woman and a Korean woman learn they were switched during IVF in an intensely controlled film from Kiyoshi Kurosawa protegé Akira Yamamoto.
articles.content: “ The Intertwining ” director Akira Yamamoto was mentored by Kiyoshi Kurosawa , and it shows. Yamamoto is one of many Japanese filmmakers to study under the legendary director of “Cure” and “Tokyo Sonata,” who was a professor at Tokyo University of the Arts from 2005 to 2023. And although he’s not Kurosawa’s most famous pupil — that would be “All of a Sudden”‘s Ryusuke Hamaguchi , whose style is also an influence here — he has clearly taken many lessons on composition and timing from his former teacher. To this end, Yamamoto’s latest feature takes a politically charged family drama and laces it with restrained, but palpable psychological tension, creating a film whose quietest moments are also its most uneasy ones. Shots in this film frequently linger just a few seconds longer than they’re “supposed” to, reflecting the pauses in dialogue scenes where characters choose their words before they speak. articles.title: Even Netflix Is Turning to AI to Help Audiences Figure Out What to Watch
articles.summary: A new function called AI Discover launches today for select users in the United States.
articles.content: You too, Netflix ? Netflix’s whole thing has been that its algorithm was designed in such a way that it knows what you’ll want to watch, that even small shows with no hype or stars like “Baby Reindeer,” “Adolescence,” “Squid Game,” “Ginny and Georgia,” or even “Stranger Things” once upon a time can turn into massive, organic hits. They call it the “Netflix Effect” for a reason. But even Netflix has had trouble keeping people consistently engaged and in getting them to find that next show or film . Last month it overhauled its creative leads to meet that challenge , so it is turning to where so many other companies have turned to shake things up: AI . Related Stories To Follow Her Best Picture Win, Siân Heder Opted to Make ‘the Hardest Story She Could Imagine’ Netflix today launched AI Discover, which is a new tab on the streamer’s TV app where you can ask an AI assistant to help you narrow down a selection based on what you say you’re in the mood to watch. Fortunately Netflix didn’t do the Meta thing and come up with some cuddly meeple to be your virtual assistant. The tool is built around themes, in which you select from a range of themes, each of which is previewed via a clip from a show or movie. You can say I want to watch “Something Light” or “Scare Me” or ask for something for families, something that’s popular, or something quick, to name a few options. The AI will give you recommendations, it will allow you to refine your selections further and you can continue doom scrolling, and you can finally “Tune Your Recommendations” to either keep a recommendation or tell the AI to not recommend it again. What this is not is an AI chat bot. You don’t even type anything into it (TV remotes are sometimes hard for that), just pick from some pre-selected options until you get what you want. articles.summary: For "Being Heumann," Heder takes on a seminal moment in the life of the remarkable disability activist Judy Heumann. She imagined a risky film, populated by all manner of disabled performers, that felt more "Dog Dog Afternoon" than cultural vegetables. All that? It was scary. It was worth it.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This interview was originally published during the 2026 Toronto International Film Festival. Apple will release “ Being Heumann ” in select theaters on Friday, November 6 and on Apple TV on Friday, November 13.] After I watched Siân Heder’s “Being Heumann” in the weeks leading up to its world premiere as the opening night film at this year’s Toronto International Film Festival , I had a long list of things to talk to the filmmaker about. Curb cuts — those graded concrete ramps at the edge of sidewalk corners that allow anyone and anything with wheels to glide gently onto the street below — aren’t really the sort of thing most people think about. But if you need them, if you’re in a wheelchair or pushing a stroller or dragging a heavy suitcase, they’re tough not to think about. It’s hard to jump off a curb if you can’t, well, jump. At best, you need help. At worst, you just can’t do it. She doesn’t really have a choice. A wheelchair user for most of her life (Heumann contracted polio as a toddler), Heumann grew into the “Mother of the Disability Rights Movement,” and the film finds her at an important crossroads. First, she needs to be able to navigate the world around her, which was simply not built for her. No curb cuts. But things are changing. When the film begins, the first U.S. federal civil rights protection for people with disabilities, Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, has been signed, but no one is putting it into actual action.
